title: Countable compactness in powers of topological groups and Ramsey theoretic variations of compactness
summary: Countable compactness need not be preserved by finite products. Motivated by compactness notions for maps indexed by finite subsets of $ω$, we introduce cascade countable compactness for arbitrary barriers. For $\mathcal B=[ω]^2$, this is the previously studied notion of being doubly countably compact. We show that, in ZFC, if $G$ is a Hausdorff topological group and $1\leq k<ω$, then $k$-cascade countable compactness of $G$ implies that $G^k$ is countably compact.
